topic: root cause of P0-A billing-enforcement recursion/CQS incident (billing-enforcement.service.ts getState/applyOverrideAndEscalation)
decision: PROXIMATE CAUSE: getState() in billing-enforcement.service.ts unconditionally called applyOverrideAndEscalation() (a real tenant_billing_state UPDATE) as a side effect of what every caller treated as a cheap read; suspendTenant()/startPaymentGrace() re-read their own before-snapshot via that same getState(), re-entering applyOverrideAndEscalation before their own UPDATE committed -> infinite recursion/stack overflow the moment a payment_grace or read_only tenant crossed the suspend threshold, so the tenant was never actually persisted as suspended (find-5e5c459f, CRITICAL, discovered by read-only audit mission-531ac553 on 2026-09-06). SYSTEMIC CAUSE: the crash was a symptom of a pre-existing CQS violation -- getState() was designed from inception to disguise a write as a read (find-adbba743/find-d45d822d, MEDIUM, logged as a SEPARATE finding in the same audit) -- and nothing in the codebase (type system, lint rule, or test) prevented a read-named method from performing a write. FIX APPLIED (uncommitted, tagged P0-A-R1 in code comments as of 2026-09-09): added readStateRaw() as a pure-read primitive and rerouted every internal mutating methods before-snapshot (suspendTenant, startPaymentGrace, activateTenant, cancelTenant) to use it instead of getState(), which removes the RECURSION -- verified 72/72 billing spec tests pass, find-8a3b2ea6 marked CORRIGIDA. THIS IS SYMPTOM RECOVERY, NOT ROOT-CAUSE RESOLUTION: getState() itself is unchanged and both of its actual external callers -- BillingEnforcementGuard.canActivate (billing-enforcement.guard.ts:60) and DunningService.processTenant (dunning.service.ts:147) -- still call getState(), which still silently executes the UPDATE on every authenticated request / every daily dunning sweep. DunningService header comment (lines 20-32) explicitly documents and designs the daily sweep AROUND this residual side effect ("nothing would ever call getState() for it otherwise") instead of removing it. find-d45d822d correctly remains open (disposition: null) and requirement req-b80f6680 acceptance criteria ac-a4e2dc8e (getState must contain no reachable write) and ac-2f8ae271 (callers call escalation explicitly; read path performs zero writes) correctly remain open with zero evidence in .claude/ops/state.json -- the mission bookkeeping is accurate; only the CRITICAL crash symptom is fixed, the MEDIUM design flaw that caused it is not. DETECTION GAP: nothing distinguishes, at the code-comment level, an audit-sourced fix (R1, R5) from opportunistic self-initiated hardening added during the same edit (R2 guard allowlist, R3/R4 billing.service canonical status authority, R6 transaction atomicity) -- all six are tagged P0-A-R1..R6 uniformly, which let a later reviewer finding (find-cc1a1cfe) discover that 3 of the P0-A-touched files already encode a design decision (no billing gate at external-reconciliation webhook boundaries) that a downstream requirement (req-90013e6a) contradicts without acknowledging it as a decision point. PREVENTION (deterministic controls, not prose): (1) Do not close req-b80f6680/mark P0-A-R1 done until getState() is actually split into a pure read plus an explicitly-invoked escalate() call at both remaining call sites, OR the residual side effect is ratified as accepted design with a pinning regression test (a getState-purity spec asserting no UPDATE/INSERT is reachable from getState()s call graph without going through an explicit escalate wrapper) -- wire this as an automated structural test, not a manual review checkbox. (2) Add a deterministic mission-archival check (ops.mjs) that fails archival unless every finding in the mission being archived has either an evidenceId-backed disposition or an explicit carry-over record in the successor mission, so find-735869b6/find-d1cb18a4-class findings cannot silently disappear during a mission handoff again (tracked as find-00018e0e).
